Name: Stephanie Beadle
Badge: Joining a Conversation
What is one insight you gained from completing the Atwoodian Table yourself that might shape how you introduce it to students?:

I really liked the metaphor and the fact that the table doesn't have "sides." I think, so often, my students have an idea of what they think and they don't really consider the nuance or even that they might be wrong. This tool gives them the opportunity to look at the different facets of a topic and synthesize the sources before adding to the conversation. I didn't feel like I needed to argue one way or another in this example, maybe I'd feel differently with a more charged topic, but I think this round table dialogue allowed me to look at different information, summarize it as I went, and then consider the valid points from each person and what I agreed and didn't agree with. I think when I use this with students I will definitely highlight the round table and the fact that they have seat at the table, too.

How does the Atwoodian Table idea compare to how you have taught argument and/or responding to multiple texts in the past?:
I've obviously presented materials that offer "both" sides to an argument, but I've never had something so smooth to aid students in synthesizing and organizing that information. Again, it's more of a two sides situation instead of a dialogue.
What do you notice about the two sets of excerpts in this module (children in fancy restaurants and toddlers and technology)? How do the excerpts work together to invite students to join the conversation? What are some conversations related to topics you teach?:
I noticed these were pretty interesting, but low stakes. I'm always looking for lower stakes but topical arguments. I usually land on AI/Tech (so the toddles and tech fits nicely) or Teen Brain/health. Just trying to avoid highly charged issues. We just did one on if college was worth it or not, but they don't really have a lot of prior knowledge on that. I think they'd be interested in these topics without having a fully formed opinion going into it. And they are both about things relevant to their age but not things they have no experience with. Well, maybe they haven't been to a fancy restaurant, but they've probably eaten out before..
